question.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the double-angle formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡2x=2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the double-angle formula for the hyperbolic sine:

$$
\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x=2\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\operatorname{cosh}⁡x
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{sinh}⁡x(1-4\operatorname{cosh}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =\int (\operatorname{sinh}⁡x-4\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\operatorname{cosh}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int (\operatorname{sinh}⁡x-2\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{cosh}⁡x-\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x+C.\end{aligned}
$$
